subject: Is the Item Category Information Function correctly defined?

messages.author: 8aacb73aef966ff7
messages.subject: Is the Item Category Information Function correctly defined?
parts:
Phil,

in your ItemInfo/ItemInfo2 functions, the category information is calculated as grad^2/P per category, and the item information (if total.info is set to TRUE) as the sum across categories:

 for(i in seq_len(x@ncat))
        info[,i] <- (dx$grad[[i]])^2 / P[ ,i]
     if(total.info) info <- rowSums(info)    
 
 for(i in seq_len(x@ncat))
            info <- info + outer(as.numeric(dx$grad[[i]]), as.numeric(dx$grad[[i]])) / P[ ,i]

Following Samejima (1969), the category information function (or item response information function) is minus the second derivative of the log of the category probability, yielding

I = (P')^2/P - P''

with I for information and P' denoting the first and P'' the second derivative of P (each carrying an index for the item and the category; see also Magis, 2015, Eq. 8).

Now, Samejima (1969, p.39, Eq. 6-7) shows that for the item information, the P'' part of the equation above can be omitted, as it sums up to zero across categories (see also O&N2006, p.69, Eq. 4.13 and above). However, this is not the case for the categories' information. Hence, shouldn't the item category information curves include the P'' part as well?

The difference is that the category information functions are (usually) unimodal if P'' is included (cf. Samejima, 1969, p.40, Fig. 6-2) but bimodal if not, thus exhibiting entirely different shapes.

Thank you,
Milica
